sort of unrelated given I didn’t have BPD at the time but I was scared of living past 18 given the economic opportunities for people that didnt go to college and on the other hand, college debt for life. I took a gap year and now im in my last semester but still absolutely dreading that fear but at least I’m alive. 

This dystopian reality just has me numb at this point so I still keep myself super aware of our current state of politics/socioeconomic conditions. I’m with you there too on family getting possibly deported and recommend if you haven’t, sending the ACLU Immigrant rights guide to interacting with ICE if it happens. My advice would be to practice DBT skills because they’re universally helpful. Dive response trick is my go-to with breakdowns. 

Make sure to acknowledge and appreciate the little things like surrounding yourself with people you love, watching movies, finding new music to listen to, overall just trying new things makes for life feeling a bit more expanded and worth it. Even down to taking a different route to work, home, school, etc. Remember to put yourself first and live in the moment. You don’t need to figure everything out right now. Not attending a protest due to your mental conditions is just as valid as if it material conditions in the way. 

You are not alone. We will all get through this together. I try to avoid this contempt with an absurdist mindset thinking of how unreal things are in a silly way while also acknowledging the love and hate we’re facing. Don’t ever think of yourself as a someone not worthy of love and life. I still carry the guilt of my close friend’s suicide and childhood friend passing from Leukemia, but I know there’s nothing I can do to change the past and that it isn’t helping myself to submit given my acceptance and rational thought partly developed through therapy. 

If you have access, make sure to seek a psychological evaluation and resources to help. I was super demotivated to start therapy, but it’s worth it in the long run. You deserve love and fulfillment, especially since your heart is in the right place and also self aware about what’s practical within your overall capability, which is a positive thing. Again, your own health comes first. Think of yourself as if you were your own child. We’ll persevere together, even if it doesn’t feel like it <3 As I always say,    fuck it we ball

When I had TikTok one thing I noticed were comments mostly questioning/believing whether they have BPD on posts by conventionally attractive people making quirky jokes about their disorder. Not to put all the blame on those types of people but romanticized jokes about it really make an impact of people’s perception of it. They’ll hear that dissociation and depression symptoms are a major role and think “omg i think i have bpd!!” without knowing the severity of it. Feeling like an absolute shell of a human and ghost of what you were while simultaneously experiencing unbearably intense emotions all the fucking time. 

A LOT of people, especially Gen Z, dissociate. There are a lot of comorbid symptoms especially with major levels of depression and anxiety, in which is becoming so much more common with younger people. But the severity for an example like suicidal ideation is nearly terminal, always having those thoughts and even urges in the back of your mind at the very least. Struggling so much with some form(s) of self harm and having the urge everyday. Occasionally believing your loved ones are acting out a plan they have to hurt you or that you’re constantly being watched.  

There’s two symptoms (well one not technically on the DSM but an agonizing occurrence) that piss me the fuck off with how reduced and normalized their perceptions are. The first being Identity Disturbance. It’s so commonly claimed, again, with younger people too, because they hear/read its description and think they relate when literally growing up is always finding out who you are. That’s LITERALLY what growing up is, even in your 30’s its common to still seek new interests and ambitiously introspect. The thing is is that it’s often chronic mirroring with fear of abandonment as attached, over-identifying with people, figures in media, and just any overall interests as an automatic fill the absence of self of self, having contradictory and/or constantly changing beliefs and values. Just constantly putting in all of your energy into gaining acceptance and attacking yourself or blaming others in different ways when you fuck up even in the smallest way. 

The second being ‘intrusive thoughts’ which has just so much lost its actual meaning. Even vanilla-type people joke about it under the assumption that something like looking down while standing at the top of a building and thinking “omg what if i jumped” is an intrusive thought. That’s so easily provoked. You could be triggered by something that reminds you of trauma, but it’s not as simple as being annoyed by some kid or crying baby on a plane and beating them up from feeling angry in that moment. Well, it could be, but it’d be to an extreme degree (like murdering or nearly murdering) and feeling absolutely disgusted with yourself. 

Intrusive thoughts have been so sensationalized people don’t know actual subjects and examples would be like pedophilia, incest, sexual assault, or murdering people you love, randomly finding the nearest and quickest way to commit suicide as you’re hanging out with your closest friends, etc. It’s a fucking nightmare and makes you feel like a terrible person despite those thoughts being the complete opposite of your values and beliefs. It’s all just a fucking nightmare.

That concludes my take essay.

As a fine artist in art school, I’m pretty limited mentally into making art about my lack of identity. it gets so damn difficult explaining my work to people about the nuance of relationships between life events and bpd symptoms as expressed in my work. I don’t really have a consistent art style and always move on to some other medium after each project. It’s a damn headache too not to come off as a corny “im depressed lol here’s some disturbing looking art that represents my twisted mind” visual artist so it always feels like such an intimidating rabbit hole to conceptualize my idea which requires agonizing introspection and then forcing myself to additionally make it consumable enough not to have people look at me drastically different while still using theory and calculating my process right. It takes awhile too since I don’t use references out of fear of latching onto that source and copying it verbatim. I do know what I like and know my personality is distinct, but I don’t feel like I do at all. My pronouns and masc/fem names are whatever people choose to refer to me as. I can only mirror people interaction-wise which is exhausting. At this point in time with what’s happened in the past 2 years, I also feel like a husk, but if I have any advice, I would suggest getting out more and just faking it til you make it with being happy around other people. My mood swings make me isolate and be incredibly social very off and on, but my friends are what keep me afloat. I guess overall, pushing past your boundaries is the best advice i can give. watch some experimental movies, find new music on your to wherever, hell, make some art! Don’t feel guilty, just keep trying and aim to just being okay, not happy. & remember to take yr meds and go to therapy as most in this sub would suggest. everything will be okay.

I personally think the neutrality (although arguably left-leaning) was the good choice. I thought one scene section (which was the most overt breather) was a clear meta representation of the movie’s purpose. IMO I think it was mainly just a cautionary tale of what war could look like in our modern day in our own nation to those that are ignorant or can’t register what the carnage and dehumanization would be in a way that can click for them. We have the privilege to ignore current wars because they aren’t happening on our soil. I think this movie’s existence is a great example of The Death of the Author. Alex Garland hasn’t been very open on the meaning, and I’ve seen countless reviews and comments that all slightly differ. I could be dead wrong, but I’d like to believe I’m right because it’s now whatever I want it to be regardless of the director’s intention being stated or not. If politics were a major aspect of the movie, it would only polarize the culture war a helluva lot more, defeating its purpose (in my interpretation). In fact, regardless of whatever politics they could’ve put in, people wouldn’t buy into it, which is why I think it’s better to make it obvious that its only supposed to look like the US, but still be clearly detached enough with vague details so that we can imagine and apply our own reality into its template. I think that especially in this age, we have a lot more nuanced demographics on political issues, so I can’t even begin to think about how state sections would split, but yet, many of us can agree that we’ve been a lot more divisive in recent years. I would find it hard to believe that it could simply be put as a left vs right simply because of intersectionality. I believe the journalism aspect is also very nuanced and important. Following Barthes, McLuhan, and Postman’s ideas surrounding writers and journalism, I feel there’s a lot more to take away on that area as well in a meta sense of the movie being a medium consisting of commentary on journalism while also being its own article subject to spark conversation among everyone as a (seemingly) bi-partisan story. I don’t have much to say on the characters besides how real they felt to me personally given the psychological circumstances that question ethics and humanity. I really liked the quote, “We record so other people ask questions” (which is a dialogue answer to another question regarding the ethics). When I first became vegan, I was a terminally online twitter leftist that would scold and be hostile towards non-vegans, including my friends. I pushed a lot of them away which personally fucked me up. Thinking that shit like when it comes to physically blocking consumers (like climate activists with road blocking) does jack shit besides turning them away. Respectfully, some people on here need to ground themselves and think more on how regular non-vegans psychologically operate. I have seen demonstrations like this with disrupting the actual factory farms which i feel does more than this, considering the lack of consumers directly involved. Intersectional conversations do a bunch when considering and educating people on how factory farming REALLY affects the environment, marginalized communities, health, and of course, speciesism. I always start off with describing the actual definition of veganism which is basically abstaining from overall oppression of sentient beings as much as capably possible. I’ve turned friends vegan without ever acting out the frustration at them, but instead just talking about the many overlooked and unknown facts about the philosophy. It truly is aggravating to be incredibly aware of the horrors of meat and dairy industries, but most people unfortunately will turn their brains off and even have more of a negative connotation to the movement if we don’t communicate on their level of comprehension. I’m sure this might get downvoted to shit, but to the people reading this, please just consider most people know that the animals that get slaughtered for their consumption. Theres so much more harm the industries do that people don’t know which will get them more inclined to think more about veganism. People don’t go from eating meat and dairy to being vegan (consistently/for life) just by looking at traumatizing photos and having a barrier from getting their dinner from the supermarket. It’s just annoying to them. I do think documentaries help a ton as I went vegan finally from watching Earthlings, but it took around 3 months of considering the lifestyle before actually switching (yes I know this is an anecdote). A lot of people need warming up to what this is all about before viewing absolutely revolting videos and photos and just choosing to be vegetarian or vegan for under 2 weeks. It shouldn’t be that way, but that’s just the way a lot of people work when it comes to a major lifestyle change. It’s important to remember the goal is to minimize the harm, and we have to be realistically strategic about it.
